steps.content: [Chief's Perspective]
MBCC vehicles rush through the curtain of rain, racing toward the estate on the outskirts of Eastside.
Emergency Alert: Banbury Estate under attack! M-value has exceeded threshold—confirmed presence of S-Class Sinner!
...We need to hurry.
At the edge of your vision, flames surge into the sky alongside a pillar of Mania. You can tell who's there.
[Background: Chaos, Sea of Fire Effect]
The fire rages. Tainted by Mania, the flames cannot be quenched by rain. They devour the Banbury estate inch by inch, burning away every last sin.

The woman emerges from the building and tries to take another step, but she stumbles. Only then does she notice the pain at her neck—the butterfly ornament has embedded itself into her body. With no more lives to feed on, it has begun devouring its host.
Mania surges in rhythm with her heartbeat, a fever pitch that invades her marrow and tears through her flesh. She can feel the pain. It's the same pain her family once endured in the flames.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Right, she did warn me about this.
"Don't get too worked up when you take your revenge, or the butterfly will lose control and devour you too."

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hehe... But how could I possibly hold back?

The blazing inferno continues to roar. No one is alive in the estate anymore, save for one figure standing amid the carnage, impossible to miss. A man in black, umbrella in hand, spots Clementine and bows his head in a greeting.

steps.speaker: Man in Black
steps.content: She sensed you activating your power, so she asked me to come and extend an offer.

steps.speaker: Man in Black
steps.content: You're far too talented to die here. Come and join her, while you still have the chance.
But Clementine simply shakes her head with a smile.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...I humbly decline. This is fine.
[CG - Vengeance]
Mania engulfs Clementine and everything around her, like a giant redwood burning in the night. She holds out her hand, watching the flames spiral up her arm before vanishing into the sky.
Those days of her past have grown far too distant—so much so that they feel like faded dreams, hazy and indistinct. Only that fire remains vivid in her mind.
Pain and rage pour from her pen, transforming into words. She can never return to the past, yet neither can she move forward.
Her enemy is dead. She has no regrets. If she had to say, then...
She places a hand on her chest, feeling the mark that connects her to ${PlayerName}. It's drawing closer, racing toward her.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You're still willing to read my stories next time...
[WHITE OUT]
Perhaps... I'll be able to write a better ending then.
[Enter Flashback Sequence]
"You can find a place like this in Eastside."

"A peaked roof, a two-story wooden building. In the backyard stands an ancient tree that rustles in the breeze." "It isn't particularly spacious." "The red paint on the roof has already begun to peel, the windows always let in drafts, and the aging stairs creak with every step."

"But none of that mattered." "The peeling paint formed pictures if you looked close enough, and the broken windows let in the cool summer breeze." "If you bounded up the stairs laughing, even the creaking wood would sound like a cheerful tune."
"This is 28 Redwood Lane. This is our home."

An elderly woman and her husband opened the orphanage together. She had no children of her own, so every homeless child who came through their doors became hers. She would always tell them to grow like the redwoods—strong, steadfast, and true to themselves.

There were a pair of sisters at Redwood. The older sister fell in love with a man who came to work there as a handyman, while the younger chose to venture out into the world. She joined the finest sand ship fleet and would bring back the latest and most exciting gifts for the children from the satellite towns whenever she returned.

The man had a volatile temper, a frightening face, and always struggled to find the right words. His appearance drove many away, but the Redwood welcomed him regardless. There, he slowly learned to open his heart and eventually fell in love.
The children would run through the courtyard and around the old tree, their laughter echoing throughout the orphanage. Only one thing—one person—could settle them down.

steps.speaker: Young Clementine
steps.content: What would you like to hear? Are there any books on the shelf you haven't read yet?

steps.speaker: Children
steps.content: We've already read them all, Miss Clementine.

steps.speaker: Children
steps.content: That one! We want to hear the story you wrote last time!

Sometimes, the storytelling sessions would attract other listeners as well. Mrs. Jones would sit in the shade, knitting, and Allison would squeeze herself right in among the children. William, though he would keep his distance, still listened all the same.

Little heads huddled together, paying close attention as their most beloved and trusted Miss Clementine told them the stories she'd written. The children would laugh, gasp in wonder, and even wipe away a tear or two as the tales unfolded.
<i>Keep going. Keep telling your stories. The adventure goes on, and the tale never ends.
<i>Your smiles are my most precious treasure, and the words I write are my path to freedom. Keep writing, Clementine. Perhaps... becoming a novelist wouldn't be such a bad dream after all.
<i>If only... I could stay like this with you all, and keep writing forever...
[White Screen for 3 Seconds, Then Slowly Transition to Small CG - Holy Light Finale 1]
Clementine slowly opens her eyes.
She finds herself on a train bound for somewhere unknown. Brilliant light spills through the window, its warmth settling over her, making her strangely drowsy.
It's almost as if she's been walking for so very long, and has finally gotten the chance to rest.

steps.speaker: Child's Voice
steps.content: ...Clementine! Miss Clementine!

steps.speaker: Child's Voice
steps.content: You promised to tell us a story! Why'd you stop?
The voices come from somewhere unknown, yet they're so achingly familiar that her eyes begin to sting.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Tell a story?

steps.speaker: Child's Voice
steps.content: Yeah! You stopped right at the best part last time—the detective was about to reveal who the real bad guy is!
Frozen memories begin to thaw and return. Yes... she had made such a promise, hadn't she?

steps.speaker: Child's Voice
steps.content: Are you okay, Miss Clementine?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Don't worry about me... I just had a very, very long dream...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: There was a great fire in the dream, and you all went away, one by one. I searched for so long, but I couldn't find any of you...
She trails off. A warm hand comes to rest gently on her head.
[Small CG - Holy Light Finale 2]

One by one, translucent figures settle down around her. A kind face, a cheerful face , a stern face... Every single one is familiar. She may claim to have forgotten, but they have long been etched in her heart.
She hears a whistle in the distance. The train is about to depart, bound for that place of eternal joy and peace.

steps.speaker: Familiar Voice
steps.content: So... will you come with us this time?

steps.speaker: Familiar Voice
steps.content: Though... there's someone outside calling for you. Looks like he's trying really hard to bring you back with him.
steps.female_content: Though... there's someone outside calling for you. Looks like she's trying really hard to bring you back with her.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Is that so?
She made a promise to wait for someone to return.
But her limbs feel impossibly heavy, as though they have been filled with lead. Her eyelids weigh down, about to close at any second now. Even the strength to speak is slipping away from her.

steps.speaker: Familiar Voice
steps.content: In that case... you should just rest for a while.
[Background - Eastside Streets - Sunrise]
By the time you reach the scene, it's already over. All you see are countless dots of light scattered across the sky—the remnants of that goddess of vengeance—and half a torn page.
You reach out and catch it. It's the manuscript page Clementine scribbled on in front of you.
Some of the ink on the page fades from the heat, revealing the original line of text beneath—
"The train finally arrives at the station. One by one, the passengers disembark from the Praeva."
"The shadows that have shrouded their hearts for far too long have finally been lifted. After all these years, they can finally step into the light and walk toward the future—"
[Small CG - Holy Light Finale 3]

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: Sleep well, child... You've been through so much...
Welcome home.
[ED]
